Minimum of three years of experience in acute care, which includes at least one year in Telemetry or Critical Care equivalent
Assessment: Collects patient data based on diagnosis, age and/or developmental age. Analyzes data collected.

Planning: Plans and prioritizes individualized care based on the assessment, utilizing nursing diagnosis, including teaching and discharge needs of the patient and family, and sets outcome goals in coordination with other disciplines. Ensures that the patient/family participates in the plan of care as able, and that plan of care addresses age-specific and cultural needs.

Intervention: Implements appropriate standards based on assessment. Prioritizes and organizes care within the allotted time frames. Coordinates discharge steps or ensures appropriate referral to address timely, appropriate discharge needs.
Evaluation: Evaluates patient's response to care. Modifies plan of care based on evaluation.

Clinical Skills: Demonstrates competency and efficiency in psychomotor skills generic to scope of practice and in those required in specific area of care. Responds effectively in emergency situations. Respects patients' rights.

Leadership: Directs care team members and ancillary staff in implementing patient care and delegates appropriately. Demonstrates effective problem identification and problem-solving methods. Plans staffing based on individual patient need as identified by acuity and/or patient priority and collects data to justify variances. Directs or modifies bed placement activities and unit team assignments based on changes in patient population.
Advanced Cardiac Life Support from the American Heart Association
Pediatric Advanced Life Support from the American Heart Association
